# `silk/system/terminal`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the size of a terminal, and switch it between its normal mode and raw mode.

## When to use
Use [`Terminal`](#Terminal) for a program that draws on the terminal or reads keys one at a time, such as
an editor, a prompt, or the REPL of a JavaScript runtime. Read the mode with [`Terminal.mode`](#Terminal.impl.mode)
before you change it, and give it back with [`Terminal.setMode`](#Terminal.impl.setMode) before the program ends.

## Details
The functions take a raw descriptor of a terminal, such as 0 for standard input. They never
open, close, or wait on the descriptor. A [`TerminalMode`](#TerminalMode) is a copy of the terminal settings
(`struct termios`); [`TerminalMode.raw`](#TerminalMode.impl.raw) returns the same settings in raw mode, as libuv and
Node.js define it: no line editing, no echo, no signals from keys such as Control-C, and reads
that return each byte at once.

## Errors
Each function fails with [`TerminalError`](#TerminalError): the native error code, such as 25 (`ENOTTY`) for a
descriptor that is not a terminal.

## Gotchas
- A raw terminal stays raw after the program ends. Give back the earlier mode first.
- Listen for `SIGWINCH` with `silk.system.signal_watch` to learn when the size changes.
- The module is empty on targets other than Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc
  on x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Ask a descriptor that is not a terminal
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.pointer { Pointer }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.system.terminal { Terminal, TerminalError, WindowSize }

@foreign(noCapture: .("fds"))
unsafe extern "C" fn pipe(fds: ?[*]mut i32) -> i32

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut fds: [i32; 2] = [-1, -1]
  if unsafe pipe(Pointer.fromMutSlice<i32>(&mut fds)) != 0 { return 1 }
  if Terminal.isTerminal(fds[0]) { return 1 }
  return match run Effect.result(Terminal.windowSize(fds[0])) {
    Result<WindowSize, TerminalError>.Success { .. } => 1
    // ENOTTY is 25 on Linux and Darwin.
    Result<WindowSize, TerminalError>.Failure { error } => if error.code == 25 { 0 } else { 1 }
  }
}
```

Import as `Terminal` with `import silk.system.terminal { Terminal }`.

## `TerminalError`


A failed terminal operation, with the native error code.

### Details
`code` is the `errno` value of the failed system call, such as 25 (`ENOTTY`) for a descriptor
that is not a terminal, or 9 (`EBADF`) for one that is not open.

## `TerminalMode`

```silk
pub struct TerminalMode
```

A copy of the settings of a terminal, from [`Terminal.mode`](#Terminal.impl.mode).

### Details
Keep the mode that you read first, and give it back with [`Terminal.setMode`](#Terminal.impl.setMode). Make a raw copy
with [`TerminalMode.raw`](#TerminalMode.impl.raw).

<a id="TerminalMode.impl.raw"></a>

### Method `raw`

```silk
pub fn raw(self: &Self) -> TerminalMode
```

Returns these settings in raw mode, as libuv and Node.js define it.

#### Details
Raw mode turns off line editing, echo, the signals from keys such as Control-C and
Control-Z, the translation of a carriage return to a newline on input, flow control with
Control-S and Control-Q, and parity checks. Characters are 8 bits, and a read returns as soon
as one byte is there. Output still turns a newline into a carriage return and a newline.

<a id="Terminal.impl.setMode"></a>

### Associated function `setMode`

```silk
pub effect fn setMode(fd: i32, mode: &TerminalMode) -> () ! TerminalError
```

Applies `mode` to the terminal `fd`, after the output that was written to it is sent.

#### Errors
[`TerminalError`](#TerminalError) with code 25 (`ENOTTY`) if `fd` is not a terminal, 9 (`EBADF`) if it is not
open, or 5 (`EIO`) if the process is in the background of the terminal.
